feedback_text.text: Just for funsies, my explanation for the pointy toes being more fertile was that perhaps the breeding grounds or area where eggs are laid required more dexterity to reach. Webbed toes may have resulted in eggs being laid in areas that were easier for predators to reach, thus fewer offspring reaching adulthood. Areas that were more difficult to reach might have been comparatively safer.
